title: Early Feeding TL Trial
official: Evaluation of Safety and Outcomes of Early Oral Feeding Following Total Laryngectomy
summary: This is a randomized, single-center phase 2 study comparing early versus delayed oral feeding after total laryngectomy. Dysphagia-related outcomes will be assessed using the MDADI preoperatively, and on postoperative days 14 (±7) and 30 (±7). Secondary outcomes include fistula requiring intervention, surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, oral feeding tolerance, feeding tube duration, nasogastric tube removal, length of stay, PSS-HN scores, and patient-reported oral rehabilitation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Subjects who have elected to undergo total laryngectomy surgery
* Subjects receiving free-tissue transfer regardless of indication for total laryngectomy
* Subjects who are English and/or Spanish speaking.
* Written informed consent obtained from the subject and the subject agrees to comply with all the study-related procedures.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Subjects who have undergone prior major head and neck surgery or radiation therapy involving the larynx (also referred to as surgical salvage patients).
* History of severe dysphagia or with current enteral feeding needs
* Subjects with intraoperative findings of incomplete mucosal closure judged by the operating surgeon to place the patient at risk for breakdown
* Subjects with evidence of flap ischemia or venous congestion on immediate postoperative assessment
* Subjects with uncontrolled post-operative bleeding from reconstruction site.
* Subjects with gross oropharyngeal contamination or infections noted at the time of surgery.
* Subjects with other intraoperative findings, at the surgeon's discretion, that would preclude safe participation in the study.
* Subjects who are confirmed to be pregnant or breastfeeding.
* Prisoners or subjects who are involuntarily incarcerated, or subjects who are compulsorily detained for treatment of either a psychiatric or physical illness.
* History of any other disease, metabolic dysfunction, clinical examination finding, or clinical laboratory finding giving reasonable suspicion of a disease or condition that contraindicates the use of protocol therapy or that might affect the interpretation of the results of the study or that puts the subject at high risk for treatment complications, in the opinion of the treating physician.

  * Including pre-existing conditions that put them at risk for poor wound healing, including: scleroderma, active AIDS (CD4 count \<200 or not on HAART therapy), autoimmune disease, organ transplant patients on immunosuppressive medications.
  * Including a history of traumatic brain injury, stroke, or dementia.
